raw_response:
*sits down with a cigarette and the notebook where I jot down what I planted last year*

Alright, let me think this through. I've got 50 mu to work, which is a decent size for our village — bigger than most of the smallholders but not like those big contract farms out near the county road. Seven people in the household, so labor isn't my biggest worry. My wife and I do most of the field work, my older brother helps when he's not driving his truck, and the kids pitch in on weekends during busy times.

**Land allocation first.** The wheat is already in the ground since last October, so that's decided — about 30 mu of wheat-maize rotation, which is my bread and butter. That 30 mu will go to summer maize right after wheat harvest in June. The other 20 mu I split across the cash crops: 5 mu garlic (planted last fall, harvesting in May-June), 4 mu stevia (that contract buyer from Anhui came through again), 4 mu cabbage, 3 mu chili, and 4 mu onion. The vegetables are where I make real money if I don't mess them up.

**Wheat (30 mu, already growing).** I put down compound fertilizer at planting last October — about 40 kg/mu of the 15-15-15 stuff, standard. Now at the green-up and jointing stage I'm topdressing urea, around 15 kg/mu. Extension said 13 is enough but my land on the west side is a bit sandy so I do a little extra. If the wheat heads out yellow I might spray a foliar urea at grain filling. Irrigating 3 times this year — green-up, jointing, and grain-fill. Pumping from the well is costing more every year, electric rates went up again. Expecting 480-500 kg/mu if no hailstorm hits us in May like two years ago.

**Maize (30 mu, planting mid-June).** Right after wheat harvest, no time to mess around. I use the no-till planter my neighbor and I share — costs me 40 yuan/mu custom rate but saves me a week. Denghai 605 seed again, it's done well for me three years running. Base fertilizer with the planter, topdress urea at big-flare stage around late July. Only irrigate if July and August are dry — last year I didn't irrigate once, rains came through. Pests I watch for are armyworm and corn borer, spray once usually.

**Garlic (5 mu, harvesting May-June).** Already in the ground since October. This is money crop — I put down manure last fall plus compound. Been watering it regularly. Prices were bad last year, lost some money, but my cousin says the market is coming back. If prices are still low at harvest I'll string some up and store it, sell later.

**Cabbage (4 mu, spring crop).** Planting transplants end of April. Heavy feeder, lots of fertilizer. Harvest late June before maize season really heats up. Need to watch for aphids and cabbage worm.

**Chili (3 mu, transplanting now).** The processing plant buys dried chili at contract price, that's my insurance. Plant Sanying variety. Moderate fertilizer, irrigate every 10-15 days in July-August. Harvest multiple picks September-October. This is labor heavy — that's where the family helps out.

**Onion (4 mu, already planted).** Spring onions planted in March, harvesting June-July. Sell at Quzhou market. Decent margin if the price holds.

**Stevia (4 mu).** The buyer supplies the seedlings and tells me roughly what to do. Low fertilizer compared to vegetables. Multiple cuttings through the summer. Not big money but steady.

**Money situation.** I saved about 25,000 yuan from last year's harvests to put into inputs. Plus I can get credit from the fertilizer dealer — I owe him from last season still but he knows me. Won't over-extend on fertilizer because if we get a drought and pumping costs eat my margins, I need cash reserves.
